questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the purification and separation techniques of organic compounds:

Statement I: Glycerol is separated from spent-lye in the soap industry by distillation under reduced pressure because it decomposes at or below its normal boiling point.

Statement II: During steam distillation of a water-insoluble organic liquid such as aniline, the aniline–water mixture boils at a temperature slightly above \(373\ \mathrm{K}\).

Statement III: Column chromatography and thin layer chromatography (TLC) are based on the principle of differential adsorption, whereas paper chromatography is a type of partition chromatography.

Statement IV: In thin layer chromatography, the retardation factor (\(R_f\)) is defined as the ratio of the distance moved by the solvent from the baseline to the distance moved by the substance from the baseline.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Purification methods such as reduced-pressure distillation, steam distillation, and chromatography exploit differences in boiling points, vapour pressures, differential adsorption, and differential partitioning between phases.

Step 2: Evaluation of Distillation Under Reduced Pressure
A liquid boils when its vapour pressure equals the external pressure. By lowering the external pressure with a vacuum pump, high-boiling liquids that decompose at or below their normal boiling points can be boiled at much lower temperatures. Glycerol is separated from spent-lye in the soap industry using this technique. Thus, the claim regarding glycerol separation is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Steam Distillation
In steam distillation of a water-immiscible organic liquid, boiling occurs when the sum of the vapour pressure of the organic liquid (\(p_1\)) and that of water (\(p_2\)) equals atmospheric pressure (\(p = p_1 + p_2\)). Since \(p_2 < p\), water boils below its normal boiling point, so the mixture boils close to but below \(373\ \mathrm{K}\). Thus, the claim that the mixture boils slightly above \(373\ \mathrm{K}\) is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of Chromatographic Classification and Retardation Factor
Column chromatography and thin layer chromatography are both forms of adsorption chromatography using a solid adsorbent such as silica gel or alumina, while paper chromatography relies on continuous differential partitioning between water trapped in the paper (stationary phase) and a mobile solvent. Thus, the classification claim is correct. However, the retardation factor is given by \(R_f = \frac{\text{Distance moved by the substance from base line }(x)}{\text{Distance moved by the solvent from base line }(y)}\), not its reciprocal. Thus, the claim defining \(R_f\) as solvent distance divided by substance distance is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Only the claims concerning the separation of glycerol by distillation under reduced pressure and the classification of column, thin layer, and paper chromatography are correct, whereas the claims regarding the boiling temperature in steam distillation and the formula for \(R_f\) are incorrect.

answer.text: Only I, II, and III are correct.
Only I, III, and IV are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q02 - IUPAC priority, metamerism, carbanion geometry, and resonance stability

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements concerning IUPAC nomenclature, isomerism, reactive intermediates, and resonance:

Statement I: In the IUPAC order of decreasing priority for functional groups, a carboxylic acid group (\(-\mathrm{COOH}\)) has higher priority than an ester group (\(-\mathrm{COOR}\)), which in turn has higher priority than an aldehyde group (\(-\mathrm{CHO}\)).

Statement II: Methoxypropane (\(\mathrm{CH_3OC_3H_7}\)) and ethoxyethane (\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OC_2H_5}\)) are metamers because they share the molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}O}\) while differing in the alkyl chains attached on either side of the functional group.

Statement III: In the methyl carbanion (\(\mathrm{H_3C^-}\)), the negatively charged carbon atom is \(sp^2\) hybridised with a trigonal planar geometry.

Statement IV: Among contributing resonance structures of a molecule, the structure with more covalent bonds, complete octets on all atoms (duplet for hydrogen), and less separation of opposite charges is more stable.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Systematic nomenclature relies on functional group priority rules, structural isomerism depends on connectivity differences, reactive intermediate geometry is governed by hybridisation, and resonance hybrid stability depends on the relative stability of canonical contributors.

Step 2: Evaluation of Functional Group Priority
In polyfunctional organic compounds, the principal functional group is chosen according to the decreasing priority sequence: \(-\mathrm{COOH} > -\mathrm{SO_3H} > -\mathrm{COOR} > -\mathrm{COCl} > -\mathrm{CONH_2} > -\mathrm{CN} > -\mathrm{HC=O}\). Therefore, \(-\mathrm{COOH}\) takes precedence over \(-\mathrm{COOR}\), and \(-\mathrm{COOR}\) takes precedence over \(-\mathrm{CHO}\). Thus, the priority claim is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Metamerism
Metamerism arises when compounds with the same molecular formula possess different alkyl chains on either side of a divalent or polyvalent functional group. Both \(\mathrm{CH_3OC_3H_7}\) and \(\mathrm{C_2H_5OC_2H_5}\) have the molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}O}\) and differ in the alkyl groups flanking the ether oxygen. Thus, the metamerism claim is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Methyl Carbanion Geometry and Resonance Stability
In \(\mathrm{H_3C^-}\), the carbon atom has three \(\mathrm{C-H}\) bond pairs and one lone pair (four electron pairs), making it \(sp^3\) hybridised with a distorted tetrahedral (pyramidal) shape rather than \(sp^2\) trigonal planar (which describes the methyl carbocation \(\mathrm{H_3C^+}\)). Thus, the claim regarding methyl carbanion hybridisation and geometry is incorrect. For resonance contributors, greater number of covalent bonds, complete octets, minimal charge separation, and proper charge distribution increase stability. Thus, the resonance stability claim is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims concerning IUPAC functional group priority, metamerism in \(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}O}\) ethers, and resonance contributor stability are correct, whereas the claim describing the methyl carbanion as \(sp^2\) hybridised and trigonal planar is incorrect.

answer.text: Only I, II, and IV are correct.
Only II, III, and IV are correct.
All four statements I, II, III, and IV are correct.
